cases.agent: aluminum phosphide (inhalational, phosphine gas from grain storage beneath residence)
cases.agent_quote: Subsequent police inquiry confirmed the use of aluminum phosphide as a pesticide in a grain storage area located beneath the family’s residence.
cases.circumstance: environmental exposure at home: strong chemical odor in the home the previous night affecting both mother and child; mother also had nausea, vomiting, and lethargy; forensic/police investigation identified pesticide in grain storage beneath the residence

symptoms.quote: A previously healthy 2-year-old girl was brought to the emergency department with vomiting, altered mental status, and respiratory distress.
A previously healthy 2-year-old girl was brought to the emergency department with vomiting, altered mental status, and respiratory distress.
A previously healthy 2-year-old girl was brought to the emergency department with vomiting, altered mental status, and respiratory distress.
On admission, the patient had a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 5–6 with preserved bilateral pupillary light reflexes.
Oxygen saturation was 88–89% while receiving 10–15 L/min of oxygen via a non-rebreather mask.

symptoms.finding: profound hemodynamic compromise (HR 180, RR 45, BP 64/26 mmHg)
symptoms.quote: Vital signs demonstrated profound hemodynamic compromise, including a heart rate of 180 beats/min, respiratory rate of 45 breaths/min, blood pressure of 64/26 mmHg, and body temperature of 36.8 °C.
Initial arterial blood gas analysis revealed severe metabolic and lactic acidosis (Table 1).

symptoms.finding: recurrent cardiac arrest due to ventricular tachycardia (two episodes, 15 min apart)
symptoms.quote: the patient experienced two episodes of cardiac arrest due to ventricular tachycardia, occurring 15 min apart
Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 30%.
Abdominal ultrasonography revealed a mildly hypoechoic and heterogeneous liver parenchyma with periportal edema, findings consistent with acute hepatitis.
progressive respiratory deterioration developed around day 20, ultimately leading to acute respiratory distress syndrome

cases.time_to_care: UNVERIFIED (brought to hospital the morning after overnight exposure; exact interval not stated)

labs.name: lactate (admission)
labs.quote: Initial arterial blood gas analysis revealed severe metabolic and lactic acidosis (Table 1).

labs.name: ejection fraction
labs.quote: Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 30%.

treatment.name: endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation
treatment.quote: prompting endotracheal intubation and transfer to the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU)

treatment.name: vasoactive/inotropic support (epinephrine, norepinephrine, milrinone, hydrocortisone, terlipressin)
treatment.quote: escalating vasoactive and inotropic support with epinephrine (up to 1 µg/kg/min), norepinephrine (up to 1.5 µg/kg/min), and milrinone (up to 0.5 µg/kg/min) infusions. A hydrocortisone bolus was administered, and terlipressin infusion was added

treatment.name: antiarrhythmics (lidocaine, amiodarone)
treatment.quote: Lidocaine bolus therapy and an amiodarone loading dose were administered for recurrent ventricular tachycardia, followed by continuous amiodarone infusion for rhythm control.

treatment.name: VA-ECMO (initiated within first 4 h; weaned day 11)
treatment.quote: emergent veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) was initiated following multidisciplinary consultation

treatment.name: continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT)
treatment.quote: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) was initiated to manage severe metabolic acidosis, acute kidney injury, and fluid overload

treatment.name: therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE)
treatment.quote: therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) was initiated. Daily TPE sessions were performed using a membrane-based system with fresh frozen plasma as replacement fluid.

treatment.name: red blood cell exchange (RBCX, two consecutive days)
treatment.quote: automated red blood cell exchange (RBCX) was performed on two consecutive days as an adjunctive therapy.

treatment.name: NaHCO3, calcium gluconate, magnesium sulfate, N-acetyl cysteine
treatment.quote: NaHCO₃, calcium gluconate, magnesium sulfate, N-asetyl cystein

treatment.name: therapeutic-dose enoxaparin after ECMO decannulation
treatment.quote: Following ECMO decannulation, therapeutic-dose enoxaparin was initiated twice daily for thromboprophylaxis

cases.outcome: died on day 21 of hospitalization after cardiac arrest despite prolonged resuscitation
cases.outcome_quote: resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful, and the patient died on day 21 of hospitalization. The exact cause of the terminal cardiac arrest could not be definitively established.
cases.notes: No gastric decontamination performed because agent unidentified at presentation. Cardiac function recovered and weaned from VA-ECMO day 11; later died of ARDS/terminal arrest day 21. Mother also symptomatic with shared environmental exposure.
